source_evidence: Because of their long-term investment horizon, an investment in a private equity fund is often illiquid and it may be necessary to hold an investment in a private equity fund for several years before any return is realized.
answer: Private equity funds often invest with a long-term horizon, typically 10 or more years. This can make an investment illiquid: investors may need to hold it for several years before realizing a return, and funds typically limit investors’ ability to withdraw their money. In other words, an investor may not be able to access that money when they choose, so the investment requires being able to wait through the relevant holding period.
